owner: sweep: numeric levers of WORLD, CAP, CKPT -- what each does at nan / inf / -inf / 0
summary: SURFACE ENUMERATED FROM THE DECLARATIONS, NOT ESTIMATED: 17 numeric levers (a Lever whose default is an int or a float and not a bool) across the three packages -- WORLD 8 of 11 declarations (lat, hid, route_d, n0, nmax, collapse_w, predict_w, horizon; enabled/feedback/grow are bools), CAP 6 of 7 (fab_start, vocab_start, lift, lift_min, pin_windows, stall_band; targets is a str with choices), CKPT 3 of 5 (every, best_keep, best_keep_tol; dir/resume are paths). 17 levers x 4 values = 68 CELLS, driven through 104 real spine.assemble.build() calls in 104 fresh subprocesses (one per configuration; CAP and CKPT levers were driven twice, once at the shipped defaults and once in an armed context -- CAP_TARGETS=both with headroom, CKPT_DIR set -- so the arms that the defaults leave unreachable were entered). Every package was then driven to its deepest executable entry point: WORLD.startup_refusals and WORLD.build (which constructs real tensors); CAP.new_valve and all three of its Gates; CKPT.saving_on, save_period (with its gate) and resume_source. FULL COUNTS OVER THE 68 CELLS: REFUSED_BY_NAME 15, REFUSED_BADLY 26, ACCEPTED_HARMFUL 0, ACCEPTED_INERT 0, ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE 8, CRASHED 0, UNREACHABLE_TODAY 19. THE ONE STRUCTURAL RESULT: src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce resolves an int lever as `int(float(raw))` inside a try/except catching only (TypeError, ValueError). nan raises ValueError and is caught, so it produces the correct self-naming LeverError. inf and -inf raise OverflowError, which is NOT caught -- so 24 of the 26 REFUSED_BADLY cells are ONE missing exception class, and it is not a property of these three packages: it is every int-defaulted lever in the tree. It also bypasses refusals the packages wrote for themselves (CKPT_EVERY=-inf never reaches CKPT's long negative-period refusal; CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-inf never reaches derive.flush_period_windows' named UnitError), and it is reachable by typing '1e999'. THE FAB_BALANCE SHAPE IS PRESENT IN CAP: src/capacity/api.py::new_valve's guard `if float(cap.lift) < 0 or int(cap.lift_min) < 0` is false for nan and for +inf, so CAP_LIFT=nan and CAP_LIFT=inf walk past a 21-line refusal written to stop a lift lowering a cap, and then die with a bare ValueError/OverflowError out of derive.lift_to when any target is armed -- or, at the shipped CAP_TARGETS=off, are accepted in silence and frozen into the Config. NOTHING ON THIS SURFACE IS ACCEPTED_HARMFUL TODAY, and the reason is the same for every candidate: the four float levers whose values would poison a tensor or invert a decision (WORLD_COLLAPSE_W, WORLD_PREDICT_W, CAP_STALL_BAND, CKPT_BEST_KEEP_TOL) all have P4 stubs as their only consumers. All twelve of those cells are UNREACHABLE_TODAY, they will arm the moment the stubs get bodies, and WORLD_COLLAPSE_W=nan is byte-for-byte the FAB_BALANCE=nan finding one package over. FOR THE RULING: a central nan/inf refusal in src/spine/lever.py would wrongly refuse ZERO cells on this surface -- no lever here declares a meaning for either value. The eight declared special values are all ZEROS, listed in legitimate_specials, and a blanket refusal of 0 would break six working mechanisms.

findings.detail:
src/spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce resolves an int lever as `v = int(float(raw))` inside a try/except that catches (TypeError, ValueError) ONLY. int(float('inf')) raises OverflowError, which is not caught, so the LeverError that would have named the lever is never built and the OverflowError propagates out of from_env, out of spine.assemble.build, and out of the entry point. Every one of the 24 cells printed the SAME nine-word message with no lever name, no value and no package:
    File "/home/user/LLM-Test/src/spine/lever.py", line 123, in coerce
      elif isinstance(d, int):    v = int(float(raw))
    OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer
THREE THINGS MAKE THIS WORSE THAN A MISSING MESSAGE. (1) +inf and -inf are INDISTINGUISHABLE: the text says 'infinity' for both, so an operator who typed a minus sign cannot see it. (2) IT BYPASSES EACH PACKAGE'S OWN REFUSAL. CKPT_EVERY has a long, deliberate, named refusal for a negative period at src/ckpt/api.py::save_period ('CKPT_EVERY=-5: a save period ... may not run backwards'); CKPT_EVERY=-inf is more negative than any value that refusal was written for and never reaches it. Same for CAP_PIN_WINDOWS, whose negative refusal lives in src/spine/derive.py::flush_period_windows and is reached from the declared coupling table at build time -- CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-20000 raises the named UnitError, CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=-inf raises the anonymous OverflowError one layer earlier. (3) THE VALUE DOES NOT HAVE TO LOOK LIKE INFINITY. Measured spellings that all reach this same line: 'inf', 'Inf', 'INF', 'infinity', '+inf', '1e999', '-1e999'. `1e999` is an ordinary-looking numeral a tired operator can type for a large cap, and it produces the identical lever-less crash.
It is a refusal, so no wrong number reaches a run -- which is why this is medium and not high. It is a defect because the tree's own idiom is a refusal that names itself, and the sibling case one line up (nan) does exactly that.

findings.detail:
THIS IS THE FAB_BALANCE=nan SHAPE, IN A SECOND PACKAGE, FOR THE SAME REASON. src/capacity/api.py::new_valve opens with the unconditional guard `if float(cap.lift) < 0 or int(cap.lift_min) < 0:` -- 21 lines of comment argue that a lift may never lower a cap -- and `float('nan') < 0` is False, so nan walks past it exactly as it walked past FAB's eleven negative-magnitude refusals.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT DEPENDS ON CAP_TARGETS, and both arms are defects of different kinds:
  * CAP_TARGETS armed ('experts'|'vocab'|'both'): new_valve dies inside the gate-building     code with a bare, lever-less `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer` raised at     src/spine/derive.py:132 in lift_to, `int(cap) + max(int(floor), int(float(frac) *     int(cap)))`. Measured through _lift_moves (CAP_FAB_START=1000) and, with the sentinel     starts, through _one_lift while rendering the cap.valve gate's arithmetic string. The     operator is told a float is NaN, not which lever they typed.
  * CAP_TARGETS=off, WHICH IS THE SHIPPED DEFAULT: nothing refuses it at all. build()     succeeds, `cap.lift` freezes as nan, new_valve returns a Valve, and all three gates     render their normal UNREACHABLE lines with no mention of the value. The nan is carried in     the frozen Config that the report will read.
The lever is a FRACTION multiplying a capacity ceiling; the only reason a nan cannot reach a cap today is that src/capacity/api.py::observe -- the one caller that lifts -- is a P4 stub.

findings.detail: The refusal fires correctly and unconditionally (at CAP_TARGETS=off too), and it names the lever and the value: `LeverError: CAP_LIFT=-inf / CAP_LIFT_MIN=8: a lift may raise this ceiling ... and may never lower it`. THE DEFECT IS THE LAST SENTENCE OF THAT MESSAGE, which is the per-operator advisory the file added on 2026-09-04 precisely so a refusal would not print only somebody else's arithmetic. It reads: 'FOR THE VALUES YOU SET: CAP_LIFT_MIN=8 is at or above 0, so at any cap at or above zero CAP_LIFT=-inf is arithmetically CAP_LIFT=0 -- set that, and the lift stays the flat +8 the floor spells.' That identity is FALSE at -inf: derive.lift_to(1000, 0.0, 8) = 1008, while derive.lift_to(1000, -inf, 8) raises OverflowError -- there is no arithmetic to be identical to. It is the false-equation-in-a-printed-message class this package has corrected in itself six times, arriving at a value the identity proof in the comment above the guard never quantified over (it reasons about finite negatives). No run reaches it, hence low.

findings.detail:
WHICH: the consuming entry point is a P4 stub -- src/world/api.py::loss_terms is `raise NotImplementedError('WORLD.loss_terms: P4 (world) fills this in')`, and `grep -n 'collapse_w\|predict_w' src/world/api.py` finds them in NO executable line anywhere in src/. Not compose()'s halt: compose reaches WORLD.build (row ~20) long before CAP.startup_refusals at row 29.
MEASURED TODAY: all six cells build cleanly, produce no warning, no gate and no refusal, and freeze the value into the Config -- e.g. WORLD_COLLAPSE_W=nan gives cfg.collapse_w = nan, world.api.build returns a live World whose every parameter is finite, and startup_refusals(ctx_tokens=64) returns [].
WHY IT IS FILED HIGH ANYWAY. These are the two multipliers on the world model's contribution to the TOTAL TRAINING LOSS. The contract for the stub is written out in its own docstring: `tot += predict_w * pop_loss(...) + collapse_w * (var + 0.04 * cov)`. The moment P4 writes that line, WORLD_COLLAPSE_W=nan is byte-for-byte the FAB_BALANCE=nan finding that caused this sweep -- a nan multiplied into `tot` makes every gradient-carrying tensor in the whole system non-finite, LM and fabric included, and nothing in this package looks at the value. inf does the same by a different route (inf * a finite loss is inf; its gradient is nan). -inf additionally INVERTS the term: a loss weight below zero turns the anti-collapse penalty into a reward for collapsing the latent, which is the one failure this subsystem's whole history is about (std 0.24 vs the code's own 'want ~1'), and it would show in a report as a spectacularly good-looking total loss.
This is a LATENT hole, not a live one, and the ruling phase should read the severity as 'what lands the day loss_terms gets a body', not as damage measurable today.

At +inf it is True forever, so every pinned flush earns a lift regardless of what the loss is doing, which is exactly the one-sided-threshold defect the band replaced (C5: three of the five expert lifts in the 0.75 GB run went to a run that was getting worse). At -inf it is False forever, same as nan.

findings.detail:
WHICH: the only consumers are src/ckpt/api.py::new_retention and src/ckpt/api.py::Retention.consider, both P4 stubs. Not compose()'s halt -- CKPT.saving_on, CKPT.save_period and CKPT.resume_source all have bodies and all ran on every cell, and none of them reads this lever.
MEASURED TODAY: all three values build and freeze (cfg.best_keep_tol = nan / inf / -inf); saving_on, save_period and resume_source return their ordinary answers at both CKPT_DIR='' and CKPT_DIR set; new_retention raises NotImplementedError.
WHAT ARMS WHEN new_retention LANDS, from the rule its docstring declares (`_cm < _prev_probe - 1e-6 and _cm <= _best * (1.0 + tol)`): at nan the second clause is False forever, so NO probe ever earns a rotation slot and the run ends holding nothing, silently -- the counters would read as 'no local lows', which is the absent-versus-inert confusion this package's DID IT FIRE surface exists to refuse. At +inf every descending probe qualifies, so the rotation fills with warm-up checkpoints and the run ends holding n snapshots of its WORST weights, which is the exact failure the lever's own declaration says it exists to prevent. At -inf the bound is -inf and nothing qualifies. Goal A rides on this: the .best snapshots are the only copies of the good model that exist (the live end-of-run model has been 1.1-1.3 b/B worse in every arm so far).

findings.detail:
WHICH: src/world/api.py::build HAS a body and ACCEPTS 0 -- it constructs a LIVE world with a zero-width latent. What is stubbed is every consumer that would then compute with it (loss_terms, forecast, manage, geometry, state_dict, load_into all raise NotImplementedError).
MEASURED: WORLD_LAT=0 builds `encoder = Sequential(Linear(64,128), Tanh(), Linear(128,0))`, `world_proj = Linear(in_features=0, out_features=64)`, `preds` of shape [6, 0, 0] and `qproj = Linear(0, 24)`; built = 'live'; counters record 'world.lat': 0; startup_refusals(ctx_tokens=64) returns []. No refusal, no gate, no warning. lat is not declared to have a zero meaning anywhere -- its help text is 'Width of the shared latent world-state', and the levers file's own section header calls lat/hid/route_d 'checkpoint geometry that is written and never checked'.
WHAT IT MEANS THE MOMENT loss_terms LANDS: the anti-collapse term is a variance over the latent, and the variance of a zero-width tensor is nan -- demonstrated with the same torch this tree runs: `torch.zeros(2,8,0).var(dim=0).mean()` -> tensor(nan). So collapse_w * nan poisons `tot` for the whole system, from a lever value that build() accepts without a word. Note also that world_proj(z) still returns a well-formed (2,8,64) tensor of biases, so the LM feedback path would be conditioned on a constant.

findings.detail:
WHICH: src/world/api.py::build accepts it (its only population guard is `if n0 > nmax`, which 0 satisfies); the consumers that would divide by the population -- loss_terms, forecast, manage -- are P4 stubs.
MEASURED: WORLD_N0=0 builds built='live', n_live=0, and an `alive` mask that is False in every one of its nmax slots ([False]*6). counters read {'world.built': 'live', 'world.live': 0, ...}. startup_refusals returns []. So the subsystem reports itself LIVE with an entirely dead population; the counter that would let a reader tell is present and correct, which is why this is medium and not higher.
The lever's own declaration argues the opposite way for keeping it: 'growth is effectively inert today ... so n0 is in practice the ONLY thing that sets how many predictors a run has'. At 0 that is zero predictors, and the routed blend over an all-dead alive mask is a division by a zero routing mass. Nothing declares 0 as an off-switch for the population -- WORLD_ENABLED=0 is that switch, and it produces a NULL world instead, which is a different and correctly-labelled object.

WHICH: src/world/api.py::build accepts it and builds the encoder as `Sequential(Linear(64,0), Tanh(), Linear(0,32))` -- a zero-width bottleneck, so the latent is the second Linear's BIAS and is identical for every input. The consumers that would notice (loss_terms' latent_std, which the levers file calls the collapse check) are P4 stubs.
MEASURED: builds clean, built='live', all parameters finite, counters carry no hid field at all so the value is not even recorded in the DID IT FIRE surface, startup_refusals returns [].
A CONSTANT LATENT IS THE SUBSYSTEM'S ONE RECORDED FAILURE MODE (std 0.03-0.15 against the code's own 'want ~1'), and WORLD_HID=0 produces it by construction with nothing said. Low rather than medium because nobody types 0 for a hidden width by accident and the value is not load-bearing anywhere else.

Under the declared test `_cm <= _best * (1.0 + tol)`, tol = 0 means 'a probe must land at or below the best seen so far to earn a rotation slot' -- the strictest coherent policy and a reasonable thing to ask for. legitimate_specials:
CAP_FAB_START=0 -- "start at the hard ceiling, i.e. no room to earn"; the fallback is the wire d_expert_slots (FAB.slots) and the literal must stay 0 because Lever.__init__ refuses a computed default. Declared: src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers.fab_start (help text) and implemented at src/capacity/api.py::new_valve. VERIFIED: builds cap_experts=4096 with origin "operator (fab_start=0, the sentinel) -> hard ceiling 4096".
CAP_VOCAB_START=0 -- same sentinel, "start at the model's row count"; fallback wire d_vocab_slots (LM.vocab_slots). Declared: src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers.vocab_start; implemented at src/capacity/api.py::new_valve. VERIFIED: origin "operator (vocab_start=0, the sentinel) -> hard ceiling 4096".
CAP_LIFT=0 -- a legal, in-range lift meaning "no proportional term, the lift is the flat +CAP_LIFT_MIN the floor spells". Declared in the body of the negative-lift refusal at src/capacity/api.py::new_valve ("CAP_LIFT=0 is in range, legal, and spells a flat +CAP_LIFT_MIN lift"). VERIFIED at CAP_TARGETS=both, CAP_FAB_START=1000: cap.valve renders "one lift -> 1008".
CAP_LIFT_MIN=0 -- legal; removes the absolute floor so the lift is purely proportional, and the resulting inert case (int(CAP_LIFT x cap) == 0) is REPORTED rather than refused. Declared: src/capacity/levers.py::CAPLevers.lift_min and the five-ways-an-arm-is-dead comment in src/capacity/api.py::new_valve. VERIFIED at CAP_TARGETS=both, CAP_FAB_START=1000: "one lift -> 1080".
CKPT_EVERY=0 -- "disables periodic saving, leaving the final save and SIGUSR1". Declared: src/ckpt/levers.py::CKPTLevers.every (help text) and given an arm of its own in src/ckpt/api.py::save_period. VERIFIED with CKPT_DIR set: "Gate ckpt.periodic_armed: armed, did not fire (0 vs 1) -- CKPT_EVERY=0 with CKPT_DIR set: 0 is this lever's declared disable-periodic-saving state".
CKPT_BEST_KEEP=0 -- "a single rotating .best and no .bestN ring"; it absorbs the old BEST_TRACK flag and 0 here means what BEST_TRACK=1 did. Declared: src/ckpt/levers.py::CKPTLevers.best_keep. VERIFIED: builds and freezes; the consumer (new_retention) is a stub, so the meaning is declared but not yet rendered.
WORLD_PREDICT_W=0 -- a real arm and NOT the same as WORLD_ENABLED=0: "enabled=False and predict_w=0.0 are not the same arm, because the second still trains the encoder under collapse_w and still builds the population". Declared verbatim at src/world/levers.py::WORLDLevers.predict_w. VERIFIED: builds a live world with predict_w frozen at 0.0.
WORLD_COLLAPSE_W=0 -- turns the anti-collapse term off while leaving the subsystem built and the prediction term priced; the ablation ladder D4 asks for. LEGITIMATE BY SYMMETRY WITH predict_w, WHOSE ZERO IS DECLARED -- collapse_w's own comment at src/world/levers.py::WORLDLevers.collapse_w does NOT spell out 0, and the ruling phase should note that asymmetry rather than infer it.
NOT SENTINELS, SAID EXPLICITLY SO THEY ARE NOT MISTAKEN FOR ONE: CAP_PIN_WINDOWS=0, CAP_STALL_BAND=0, CKPT_BEST_KEEP_TOL=0, WORLD_LAT=0, WORLD_HID=0, WORLD_ROUTE_D=0 and WORLD_N0=0 are all ACCEPTED by live code and NONE of them is declared to mean anything at its own declaration. WORLD_HORIZON=0 and WORLD_NMAX=0 are the two zeros on this surface that are explicitly REFUSED by name.
ON inf AS "NO CAP": no lever on this surface declares inf to mean anything. The two levers where "no cap" would be a natural reading (CAP_FAB_START, CAP_VOCAB_START) spell it as the sentinel 0 instead, and both are ints, so inf cannot even be resolved. A central refusal of nan/inf in src/spine/lever.py would wrongly refuse ZERO cells on this surface.
